description: Walk the citation graph one hop from a seed work. Direction picks the edge: incoming citations (`cites`), the seed's own references (`cited_by`), or OpenAlex's algorithmically-related works (`related_to`). Note: `direction` follows OpenAlex's filter convention, which inverts the common English reading — `cites` returns works that cite the seed; `cited_by` returns works the seed cites. Results use the works schema; combine with filters/sort to narrow further. A page holds `per_page` works and `next_cursor` continues it.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response. Pass to get the next page. Omit it on the first call — an empty string is rejected, since a supplied-but-blank cursor is a caller mistake rather than a request for the first page.

direction.description: "cites": works that cite seed_id (incoming citations). "cited_by": works that seed_id cites (its reference list). "related_to": OpenAlex algorithmically-related works (~8-30 typical, may be empty for less-cited seeds).

filters.description: Additional filter record object to narrow the graph, using the same value syntax as openalex_search_entities; native string input is unavailable here. Example: publication_year=">2020", is_oa="true". Country fields take ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes ("DE") and `language` takes ISO 639-1 codes ("en"); alpha-3, numeric, ISO 639-2, and English-name forms are converted — a multi-word name is one value, so "South Korea|Japan" ORs two countries — and a value that cannot be a country code is rejected. A multi-word value on a field matched as whole text (display_name, awards.funder_display_name, authorships.institutions.geo.city, raw_affiliation_strings) matches as one phrase ("National Science Foundation"; a comma, as in "University of California, Berkeley", is part of it, and it cannot contain a double quote of its own), "!" and "|" included, but cannot be ANDed with "+" in the same field. A value sent unquoted must have paired double quotes; balanced search phrases remain valid. Filters are checked before the seed lookup. A value mixing "|" with an AND operator — a "+", or a space on a field where words mean AND — is rejected, since OpenAlex drops every "|" alternative that ANDs more than one value; put the AND in a second key instead. Do not include cites/cited_by/related_to, nor an alias of one such as cited_works — those keys are set by the `direction` parameter.

per_page.description: Results per page. Default 25; a larger value returns at most 100 and says so (rejected instead on a server set to OPENALEX_CLAMP_PER_PAGE=false).

seed_id.description: Seed work identifier. Accepts OpenAlex work ID ("W2741809807", or its OpenAlex record-page or API URL such as "https://openalex.org/works/W2741809807"), DOI ("10.1038/nature12373" or full URL), or PMID ("12345678" or "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12345678"). A PMCID is recognized too, bare or as a PubMed Central URL, but OpenAlex indexes no PMCIDs, so it resolves nothing — pass the work's PMID or DOI instead. Use openalex_resolve_name first if you only have a title.

select.description: OpenAlex work field names to return. Always returned: id, display_name. Defaults to the curated works select if omitted. `author_list` returns each author in authorship order as `{id, display_name, orcid}` (`orcid` null when absent), a compact alternative to `authorships`, which also carries institutions and affiliations; neither the default nor `["*"]` includes it. A wide projection on a large page makes a large response, so name the fields you need.

sort.description: Sort field. Prefix with "-" for descending. Comma-separate for a multi-key sort, applied left to right, with the "-" prefix set per key ("-publication_year,cited_by_count" sorts by year descending, then citations ascending). Common: "cited_by_count", "-publication_date". Default is OpenAlex relevance.

name: openalex_get_citation_graph

budget.description: What this call cost against the OpenAlex daily budget and what is left of it. Price a full walk before committing to it: `totalCount` ÷ `per_page` × `costUsd` against `remainingUsd`. Absent when OpenAlex omitted the accounting headers.

costUsd.description: USD this call spent, covering both upstream requests — the seed validation lookup and the graph page itself. The seed lookup is unbilled unless seed_id carries characters past the identifier itself (`W2741809807#x` still resolves to W2741809807), which OpenAlex bills like one list request.

prepaidRemainingUsd.description: USD left in the prepaid balance — a separate pool OpenAlex draws on only after the daily allowance runs out, and which the daily reset does not refill. Add it to `remainingUsd` for the full spendable amount. Absent when the account holds no prepaid balance.

remainingUsd.description: USD left in today's OpenAlex budget after this call.

resetsInSeconds.description: Seconds until the daily budget refills (midnight UTC).

echo.description: Compact echo of seed_id, direction, filters, sort — surfaces what was actually queried when no edges are returned.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `unmatched_quote_in_filter_value`: A filter value sent unquoted has an unmatched double quote. `rate_limited`: OpenAlex throttled the request for exceeding its per-second ceiling (HTTP 429). `upstream_budget_exhausted`: The OpenAlex daily usage budget is spent (HTTP 429). `upstream_plan_required`: A filter is one OpenAlex serves only on a paid plan — created_date, updated_date, or a from_/to_ form of either (HTTP 429 "Plan upgrade required"). `upstream_timeout`: OpenAlex did not respond within the request deadline. `upstream_unavailable`: OpenAlex was unreachable or unusable — HTTP 503, a connection failure, or a body that was empty, HTML, or unparseable JSON. `upstream_unauthorized`: OpenAlex rejected the API key (HTTP 401). `upstream_forbidden`: OpenAlex denied access to the requested resource (HTTP 403). `comma_in_filter_value`: A filter value contains a comma, which collides with the OpenAlex filter separator, on a field that takes no phrase. Free-text search filters (any `.search` key, such as title.search or abstract.search.exact) and fields matched as whole text (display_name, awards.funder_display_name, awards.funder_award_id, authorships.institutions.geo.city, authorships.institutions.geo.region, raw_affiliation_strings, biblio fields) are exempt: a comma there is sent quoted, as part of the phrase. `invalid_country_code`: A country filter (a key ending in country_code, country_codes, or countries) holds a segment that cannot be a country code, such as a misspelled name, an unassigned number, "unknown", or two codes joined by a space ("DE US"). `mixed_and_or_in_filter_value`: A filter value puts "|" (OR) beside an AND operator — a "+", or a space on a field where words mean AND (on a country field a space is always part of a country name, and inside a language name it is part of the name). OpenAlex splits the value on "|" first and drops every alternative that ANDs more than one value, so no single value can carry both. `quote_in_filter_value`: A filter value sent to OpenAlex double-quoted holds a double quote inside its outer pair — a value the server quotes (a multi-word value on a field matched as whole text, or a value holding a comma on such a field or on a free-text search filter), or one the caller wrapped in double quotes on any filter but a free-text search. `upstream_invalid_params`: OpenAlex rejected an invalid filter, select, or sort field name (HTTP 400). `upstream_invalid_id_value`: An entity-ID filter received a value that is not an OpenAlex ID — usually a name (HTTP 400). `upstream_sort_requires_search`: sort=-relevance_score was used but the citation-graph query has no active search (HTTP 400). `upstream_invalid_params_other`: OpenAlex rejected the request (HTTP 400) for a reason other than an invalid field name. `reserved_filter_key`: filters contains cites/cited_by/related_to, or an alias of one such as cited_works — the direction parameter reserves those keys. `id_type_mismatch`: seed_id is a native OpenAlex ID of another entity type — an author, source, institution, topic, publisher, funder, award, or concept ID rather than a work ID. `id_dot_segment`: seed_id holds a `.` or `..` path segment, written plainly or percent-encoded. `entity_not_found`: OpenAlex has no work matching the seed_id. `response_too_large`: The response's structuredContent or content[] text would exceed 8,000,000 bytes — a wide `select` on a large page. A page is never shortened to fit. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

count.description: Total edges from seed_id in this direction (across all pages).

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; pass it back unchanged as `cursor`. null when no further page exists, except on a final page that exactly fills `per_page`: OpenAlex still returns a cursor there, and it leads to an empty page.

per_page.description: Page size OpenAlex echoed for this request — the applied per_page after clamping, not the number of records returned. A short or exhausted page carries fewer records than this.

notice.description: Guidance notice. Set when per_page was clamped (requested and applied sizes), when no edges are returned — a first call suggests verifying the seed_id, broadening filters, or trying a different direction; a cursor continuation says the walk is already past its last edge — and when a work carries exactly 100 authorships or author_list entries (possibly capped). Absent otherwise.

results.description: Works on the citation graph in this direction. Text values are plain text — HTML entities decoded, HTML/JATS/MathML markup removed — except identifier and URL fields such as `id`, `doi`, `ids`, and `*_url`, returned exactly as OpenAlex stores them; an abstract arrives reconstructed as `abstract`, and a selected `author_list` as one `{id, display_name, orcid}` entry per author. Possibly capped author arrays are in `windows`.

items.description: A single OpenAlex work record on the citation graph. Additional fields vary by `select`.

display_name.description: Work title. null when OpenAlex holds no title for the record (paratext works and other untitled entries) — use `id` to identify it.

totalCount.description: Total edges from seed_id in this direction across all pages.

windows.description: Author arrays possibly capped at 100 on a list record or 5,000 stored on a singleton, and the window of every `slice` call — present even when the slice holds the whole array. A slice window's `next` repeats its `slice.limit` from the following offset; `next` is null at the stored-array end, including a possibly capped singleton.

items.description: An array returned in part, or possibly in part.

next.description: `id` + `slice` call for the next elements; null at the array end.

offset.description: Index of the first element shown.

possibly_capped.description: True for exactly 100 authorships or author_list entries on a list record, or 5,000 on a singleton lookup: the byline may be longer than the returned array.

total.description: Stored array length returned to this call, not a complete byline total.

title: Openalex Get Citation Graph
